mathematical_or_operational_scope: Dual chart at general n: build C with globally separated lower/upper generators and force one row and one column family of anchored B minors to vanish. Remaining count is (n-3)(n-4).
positive_controls: Lines 30–46 check input parameter count, endpoint values, permutation set convention and S anchors. Lines 58–59 verify the constructed linear identities.
Lines 66–69 cast NumPy entries to Python int before minor products. The main test explicitly labels elimination only.

findings.issue: F and C are NumPy int64 arrays and F@C still accumulates in int64. Converting sampled y to Python ints does not remove matmul overflow. A sufficient safety condition is n*(p-1)^2<=2^63-1; the hard-coded n<=16,p<=65537 cases satisfy it, but arbitrary larger API inputs are not guarded.

No prime/root-order validation, n-domain bound, or exact permutation length/uniqueness check is made. Set equality of perm[2:] allows duplicate extra entries; it is not a complete permutation validator.

Neither C invertibility, B corner nonzeros, nor inverse-C corners are checked. Anchored minors alone cannot certify separated rank one when anchors vanish. This agrees with elimination-only labeling but prevents upgrading the return value to a factorization certificate.
assert any(remaining) intentionally rejects accidental solutions and necessarily fails in tiny n regimes with no remaining equations. This is a non-solution control, not a solution search.

cost_and_scaling: Constructs dense C and F with O(n^2) storage, O(n^3) conventional matrix multiplication, and O(n^2) anchored-minor tests. Root search and primality-factor trial division add preprocessing. It supplies no sub-FFT end-to-end implementation.
test_scope_and_limits: Main covers n=8,16 and primes 12289,65537, forty attempts each, with at least one successful chart sample required. No source executed. Safety bound checked analytically for this fixed test range.
certificate_acceptance: Returns partial charts with correct selected identities when arithmetic assumptions hold. Full certification requires all remaining minors, nonzero B anchors, det(C), inverse-corner guards, valid roots and overflow-safe arithmetic.
